tldr: The money in AI applications is moving to agents: the tools to build, secure and run them, and apps where agents do the work.
context:
Corma, which builds AI for cybersecurity, raised a $125M Series A at a $1B valuation, three months after announcing a $60M seed. LangChain, whose framework many teams use to build agents, raised a reported $300M led by Alphabet's CapitalG at a $3B valuation.

In the same week, AI hiring platform Mercor raised $750M, bringing its total to $1.2B, with Apollo, Benchmark, General Catalyst and NVIDIA among the investors.
whyPM:
Agent tooling is consolidating fast. The frameworks, eval and security tools you pick now may be bought, re-priced or turned into platforms within a year.

Keep your agent stack swappable: thin adapters over frameworks, your own eval sets, and no hard lock-in to one vendor's runtime.
bull: Well-funded tooling gets better quickly, and buyers benefit from competition between agent platforms.
bear: Valuations set three months after a seed assume huge growth; if agent adoption is slower, some of these tools will be sold or shut, leaving customers to migrate.
unknowns: How much of this revenue is real enterprise spend vs. pilots?
Will LangChain-style frameworks become features of the big model labs?
watch: Lab-native agent frameworks competing with independents
